name: Tax Structuring and Planning
title: Tax Structuring and Planning
answer: Tax structuring and planning covers the design of a group's legal entities, contracts and cash flows so that tax outcomes follow the commercial substance of a business. It spans entity choice, transfer pricing between related parties, holding and financing structures, and the timing of income and deductions across borders. In practice it sits between the tax function, legal, treasury and the finance team, and it is judged against both the tax written down and the commercial result. The work is continuous rather than annual, because structures are set up, tested and unwound as operations change.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Tax structuring and planning covers the design of a group's legal entities, contracts and cash flows so that tax outcomes follow the commercial substance of a business. It spans entity choice, transfer pricing between related parties, holding and financing structures, and the timing of income and deductions across borders. In practice it sits between the tax function, legal, treasury and the finance team, and it is judged against both the tax written down and the commercial result. The work is continuous rather than annual, because structures are set up, tested and unwound as operations change.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on the general ledger and the consolidation system, on entity management records that list every company in the group, and on the intercompany agreements that support each flow of goods, services, royalties or finance. Tax authorities increasingly receive structured data through country by country reporting and digital filing, so the same figures must reconcile from the ledger to the return. Practitioners work in spreadsheets and in dedicated tax provision and transfer pricing tools, and larger groups keep a documented policy for each material intercompany arrangement. The quality of the structure depends on the quality of the underlying accounting data more than on any single tax tool.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The method starts with the facts: who does what, where decisions are made, where risks sit and where value is created. From there the team models the tax cost of alternative structures, checks each against domestic law and treaty provisions, and documents the reasoning before anything is implemented. Transfer pricing analysis sets an arm's length price for intercompany dealings, usually by benchmarking against comparable transactions. Implementation then runs through board approvals, contract changes, registrations and filings, with the tax position monitored as rates, rules and business activity change.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Governance rests on disclosure, documentation and the allocation of risk. Most large groups operate under a tax control framework, with board level ownership of tax policy, a named responsible person and escalation routes for uncertain positions. Rules such as country by country reporting, mandatory disclosure regimes and economic substance requirements mean a structure that exists only on paper is exposed, and penalties can attach to the advisers as well as the taxpayer. Records of advice, board minutes and intercompany agreements are the evidence that a position was reasonable when taken. Nothing here is legal, tax or financial advice, and any specific position depends on the facts and the jurisdictions involved.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward more transparency and less room for structures that lack commercial substance. Multilateral reform has been shifting taxing rights toward market jurisdictions and setting a floor on effective rates for large groups, while national rules on interest deductions, hybrid arrangements and controlled foreign companies continue to tighten. Tax administrations are using data matching and analytics to spot inconsistencies between filings, which raises the value of clean, reconciled records. For teams, the practical effect is that planning is moving from one off restructuring toward continuous monitoring of a structure against changing rules.
